text:
rebecca: Heads up — after the v2.3.1 runtime rollforward at ~08:10 UTC we're seeing a sustained p95 increase (~120ms -> ~260ms) for some tenant traffic. p99 also nudged. Customers reporting higher tail latency on long sequences (>512).

jordan: Confirming. Alerts started at 08:17. Affected cohort: embeddings+generation mixed load, region eu-west-1. Any recent kernel or scheduler changes in that rollout?

rebecca: rollout included kernel-sched tweak + quant encoder micro-optim. Release notes: minor scheduler weighting change.

deploy-bot: Deploy v2.3.1 -> runtime-cluster-4 completed at 08:09:58 UTC. Canary passed.

opsbot: Observability hint: p95 delta correlates with increased queueing on hotpath queue id 17. Sampled traces show extra 1-2ms per KV lookup but amplified by batching behavior.

tasha: Quick check — can we get histogram slices by sequence length and by route? I pushed a small query to observability: `/metric/p50-p99?cohort=sequence_len:>512,route:gen`

jordan: Results: p50 unchanged, p95 jumped only for seq_len>512 and tenant cohot=acme-inc and internal test tenants. p99 shows broader noise.

sam: Repro plan: run synthetic replay with seq_len 768/1024 against v2.3.1 nodes and previous stable (v2.2.9) with identical traffic shape. Add debug tracing for kernel-sched and kvcache metrics. I can run in ~20m.

rebecca: Do we have a hotpatch option? If repro confirms scheduler change, we should either route traffic back to v2.2.9 or disable weighting.

opsbot: Temporary mitigation options: 1) route long-sequence traffic to stable runtime variant, 2) decrease max batch window for those routes, 3) enable per-tenant kvcache warmup for affected tenants.

jordan: Can we A/B route 10% of affected tenants to v2.2.9 now to compare? Need to avoid a full rollback if possible.

tasha: I've started the A/B routing split for cohort=acme*. 10% -> v2.2.9. Observability will show diff in ~5m.

rebecca: Also check kernel scheduler metrics: `sched_weight`, `queue_depth_hot`, `latency_kv_lookup` from 08:00-08:30. If weight change increased contention for long-seq jobs that's likely culprit.

sam: Running replay now against both versions. Attaching quick log snippet when done.

(replay results posted) sam: Replay done. v2.3.1 shows +140ms p95 for seq=768, v2.2.9 stable. Trace shows extra ctx-switch on hotpath after scheduler weighting increased.

jordan: Good repro. Recommendation: patch scheduler to previous weight or deploy quick rollback of that micro-change. Can we hotpatch scheduler config without rolling runtime binary?

rebecca: Ops — if we can hotpatch config, do that. Otherwise rollforward rollback on the scheduler change only. Priority: reduce customer impact asap.

opsbot: I created incident ticket INC-8421 and started an autonomous rollback window for scheduler weights.

deploy-bot: Hotpatch scheduled: change `scheduler.weight.hotpath` -> 0.65 (previous 0.85). Rolling to cluster-4 starting 08:42 UTC.

rebecca: After hotpatch metrics show p95 returning near baseline for seq>512. p99 improved but still monitoring.

jordan: Patch seems to have removed the extra ctx-switch pattern in traces. Leaving 10% A/B for 10m to validate. :thumbsup:

rebecca: Action items: 1) revert scheduler tweak permanently in next runtime bump, 2) add targeted synthetic replay to release e2e checklist, 3) long-seq cohort tests during canary. Owners: sam (replay) + tasha (canary checklist) + rebecca (release note + rollback PR).

sam: I'll open PR to revert scheduler weighting and add a regression test.

rebecca: Thanks team — closing immediate escalation. Will update postmortem if anything else turns up. :white_check_mark:
